_meta.indication: Topical treatment of onychomycosis of the toenail(s) due to Trichophyton rubrum and Trichophyton mentagrophytes

pivotal_trials.population: Subjects aged 18-70 with clinical diagnosis of onychomycosis, 20-50% involvement of target toenail without dermatophytomas or lunula involvement, positive KOH and positive culture
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Complete cure at Week 52 (0% clinical involvement of target toenail plus negative KOH and negative culture)
pivotal_trials.result: Complete Cure 117 (17.8%) efinaconazole vs 7 (3.3%) vehicle, p<0.0001

pivotal_trials.result: Complete Cure 88 (15.2%) efinaconazole vs 11 (5.5%) vehicle, p<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >1%) were ingrown toenail (2.3% vs 0.7% vehicle), application site dermatitis (2.2% vs 0.2%), application site vesicles (1.6% vs 0.0%), and application site pain (1.1% vs 0.2%)
target_moa: Azole antifungal that inhibits fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase involved in the biosynthesis of ergosterol, a constituent of fungal cell membranes

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the drug

description.text: Added labeling for use in pediatric patients ages 12 to less than 17 years based on study V01-108A-401

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for labeling changes to reflect the outcome of study V01-108A-401 conducted in pediatric subjects ages 12 to less than 17 years and to comply with Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule (PLLR).

summary.text: Jublia was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA for a new molecular entity triazole antifungal, reviewed under Standard review. The original application received a Complete Response in May 2013 for CMC deficiencies (container closure leakage), and was approved on the second cycle after those issues were resolved. It was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: Dow Pharmaceutical Sciences submitted a 505 (b)(1) New Drug Application for JUBLIATM (trade name pending approval), efinaconazole solution, 10%, with a proposed indication of once daily topical treatment of onychomycosis of the toenail in adults. The proposed product is a new molecular entity in the United States, and is not marketed in any other country.
Application Type 505(b)(1)Application Number(s) 203-567Priority or Standard Standard

The original NDA was submitted on July 26, 2012 and this submission received a complete response due to Chemistry Manufacturing and Control (CMC) deficiencies on May 13, 2013, principally related to leakage of the container closure system

Your application for Jublia (efinaconazole) topical solution, 10% was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the drug in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of a disease.
